Boyhood of Christ
BOI-hood uhv KRYST
proper noun
The childhood and youth of the Lord Jesus at Nazareth, chiefly the scene of the boy in the temple (Luke 2:40–52).

📖 Biblical Definition

The boyhood of Christ is the hidden growth of the Lord Jesus from infancy to manhood at Nazareth, of which the Gospels give one luminous scene: the boy of twelve in the temple at Jerusalem. Scripture says the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him—a true and real human development, the eternal Son growing as a boy. At twelve, lingering in the temple after the feast, He was found among the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions, and all that heard Him were astonished at His understanding. To His mother’s gentle reproach He gave His first recorded words: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?—the dawning consciousness of His unique Sonship and mission. Then He went down with them and was subject unto them, the perfect Son honoring His earthly parents; and Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. The dictionary reads the boyhood of Christ as a window into the reality of the incarnation: the Son of God was truly a boy, who grew, learned, obeyed, and was subject to His parents, sinless in every stage, fulfilling all righteousness even in childhood—true God and true man from the cradle, growing toward the cross.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The childhood of the Lord Jesus at Nazareth, chiefly the boy of twelve in the temple; the eternal Son truly growing in wisdom and stature, sinless and subject to His parents.

BOYHOOD OF CHRIST, the childhood of the Lord Jesus at Nazareth.

The child grew and waxed strong, filled with wisdom (Luk 2:40).

At twelve, found in the temple among the doctors, astonishing all.

His first recorded words: I must be about my Father’s business (Luk 2:49).

He was subject to His parents and increased in favour with God and man.

📖 Key Scripture

Luk 2:40 — "And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him."

Luk 2:49 — "And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

Luk 2:51 — "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart."

Luk 2:52 — "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The apocryphal infancy gospels invent fanciful childhood miracles, and modern readers deny the reality of His growth; Scripture shows a real, sinless boyhood, true God and true man.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Two errors touch the boyhood of Christ. The first is the apocryphal one: the so-called infancy gospels, rejected by the church, fill His childhood with grotesque and fanciful miracles—the boy striking playmates dead or making clay birds fly—legends that contradict the sober Gospel record and the sinless character of the Lord. The second is the modern denial of the reality of His growth, as though true deity could not truly learn or develop; but Luke plainly says He increased in wisdom and stature. The canonical Gospels give one restrained, luminous scene, and we are not to add to it the inventions of pious fancy.

The principle to recover is the reality of the incarnation from the cradle. The eternal Son was truly a boy—He grew, waxed strong, was filled with wisdom, asked and answered questions, and was subject to His parents—yet without sin, fulfilling all righteousness even in childhood. His first recorded words reveal the dawning consciousness of His Father’s business, and His obedience at Nazareth fulfilled the fifth commandment perfectly on our behalf. He was true God and true man at every stage, the obedient Son whose whole life, boyhood included, was a sinless righteousness reckoned to His people.
